subject: dropping original data locations from model output

messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: dropping original data locations from model output
parts:
I'd like to share my model output with colleagues, but the models use geocoded patient data that I cannot share.

So I would need to create an object that drops the original data locations but preserves the remainder of the output. Is there any way to do this?

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] dropping original data locations from model output
parts:
I'm not sure of all the things you would have to remove.

At least: Remove $.args !

I would suggest the opposite approach, make a new list, with only the fields you really need them to have, like summary.random summary.fixed summary.hyper etc. And make sure that these objects do not contain sensitive information.

Kind regards,
Haakon

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] dropping original data locations from model output
parts:
I second Haakon's suggestion, and add another note:

In a spatial model, the posterior standard deviations themselves (and certainly the posterior precision matrices, so any $config output used for posterior samples for example) can reveal the locations of the data; if the data points are scattered and isolated, one can reverse-engineer them, since the posterior precision matrix is essentially of the form Q+A' Qe A, where Q and Qe are determined by the estimated model parameters (and therefore known) and A encodes the data locations. The diagonal of the precision, or the diagonal of its inverse (the posterior variances) are enough to locate isolated data locations. You'll have to decide whether this is a realistic enough risk in your situation.

This general problem is seeing a lot more research now, but I don't think I've seen anyone specifically address this version of the issue.

Finn
